stem: A sales dashboard at Marlowe Foods takes 40 seconds to open. It holds 30 visuals, each running its own query. What is the best first fix?

options.text: Reduce the number of visuals per page
Add more filter slicers to the report
Switch every chart to a 3D style
Email a static copy to each viewer

explanation: Fewer visuals means fewer queries run on load, so the page opens faster. More slicers add more queries, 3D styling adds rendering work, and emailing copies avoids the problem instead of fixing the dashboard.

stem: A report built on a live connection loads slowly every morning when 200 people open it. The data changes only once a day. Which change helps most?

options.text: Query the source tables again on every click
Cache results or import a daily extract
Add a second copy of the live report
Disable all report-level filters

explanation: Caching or importing an extract serves the same daily data without hitting the source repeatedly. Querying on every click makes load worse, a duplicate report doubles the demand, and disabling filters does not reduce source queries.

stem: A dataset refresh at Tern Logistics takes six hours because it reloads ten years of history nightly. Only the last week changes. What should the analyst configure?

options.text: A full refresh twice each night
A longer timeout on the connection setting
Incremental refresh of recent partitions
A wider table with extra columns

explanation: Incremental refresh reloads only new or changed partitions, which cuts the time sharply. Running full refreshes more often makes it slower, a longer timeout only hides the delay, and extra columns add data to move.

stem: Two scheduled refreshes of the same dataset overlap, and the second one fails with a lock message. Which action fixes this pattern?

options.text: Delete the older refresh history
Add more visuals to the report
Rename the dataset to a shorter, clearer name
Stagger the schedules so they do not overlap

explanation: Spacing the schedules lets each run finish before the next starts, so the lock does not occur. Deleting history does not change timing, more visuals add load, and renaming a dataset has no effect on locking.

stem: A file feeding a report has grown to eight gigabytes, and the report slows down. The report uses only 6 of the file's 90 columns. What is the best action?

options.text: Remove unused columns before loading
Load every column and hide the unused ones
Convert every number to text
Duplicate the file for backup

explanation: Dropping columns before load shrinks memory use and load time. Hidden columns are still loaded, text values usually take more space than numbers, and a duplicate adds storage without helping the report.

stem: A report on three years of individual transactions is too large to refresh quickly, yet users only view monthly totals. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Add a column for each transaction type
Pre-aggregate the data to monthly totals
Raise the report page size
Store the rows in a text file

explanation: Summarizing to the level users need reduces row count and speeds queries. Adding columns grows the data, a larger page size changes layout only, and a text file is usually slower to read than a structured table.

stem: A manager picks the region North in a slicer, but the table still shows all regions. What is the likely cause?

options.text: The table has too many rows
The chart title is too long
The slicer's interactions with that table are off
The slicer's font is set too small to read

explanation: If interactions are disabled, the slicer does not pass its selection to the table. Row count, title length and font size do not affect whether a filter applies.

stem: A filter on order date returns no rows even though orders exist for that month. The date column was imported as text. What is the best fix?

options.text: Increase the page refresh rate
Sort the column in descending order
Hide the column from the report view on each page
Change the column to a date data type

explanation: Filters on dates need a true date type, so converting the column lets the range comparison work. Refresh rate, sort order and visibility do not change how the filter reads the values.

stem: A status filter for Active returns 480 customers, but the source holds 500. Twenty rows contain Active with a trailing space. How should the analyst correct this?

options.text: Trim whitespace in the column during cleaning
Round the customer count upward
Rename the column to Status2
Filter on the customer name instead of status

explanation: Trimming makes the values match exactly, so every Active row passes the filter. Rounding changes the count without fixing it, renaming the column does not touch the values, and filtering on name answers a different question.

stem: A dashboard showing store inventory has displayed the same numbers for three days. What is the most likely reason the data is stale?

options.text: The chart colors were reset
The refresh job fails, so no new data loads
The slicer lists too many values to scroll
The report has too few pages

explanation: A failed scheduled refresh leaves the last successful data in place, which looks current but is old. Chart colors, slicer size and page count do not stop new data from loading.

stem: A report shows yesterday's sales to users who open it before 9 a.m., although the source updates at 6 a.m. The refresh is set for 5 a.m. What should change?

options.text: Hide the last-updated timestamp
Delete the cached copy and rebuild it hourly
Schedule the refresh after the source finishes updating
Remove the date slicer

explanation: Running the refresh once the source has updated means the report picks up the latest data before people open it. Hiding the timestamp conceals the issue, rebuilding the cache hourly still misses the 6 a.m. source update because it does not wait for that load, and the date slicer is unrelated.

stem: After a file load, a name column shows garbled characters, such as accented letters replaced by symbols. Which cause is most likely?

options.text: A missing chart legend
An overly wide dashboard
A slicer set to allow multi-select values
A character encoding mismatch during import

explanation: Reading a file with the wrong encoding corrupts non-standard characters. A legend, dashboard width and slicer mode affect display or filtering, not how file text is decoded.

stem: A nightly file from a vendor arrives cut off halfway through, and the report totals are far too low. What is the best validation step?

options.text: Compare the file's row count to the source count
Switch every visual to a bar chart style
Add a title to the dashboard
Sort the report by date

explanation: Comparing counts shows the file is incomplete before it reaches users. Chart type, titles and sorting do not detect missing rows.

stem: A report shows revenue that does not match the finance system. Which technique best finds out which figure is right?

options.text: Reformat the numbers with commas in the service
Source validation against the system of record
Apply a new color theme
Increase the font size of totals

explanation: Checking the report's figures against the system of record shows where they diverge. Formatting, themes and font size change appearance without testing accuracy.

stem: An analyst narrows a slow, wrong-looking report to one customer segment and sees the numbers become correct. What technique is this?

options.text: Branding the report
Adding data labels
Data filtering to isolate the problem
Publishing to more users on each page

explanation: Filtering to a smaller subset isolates where results go wrong. Branding, labels and wider publishing do not help locate a fault.

stem: Before release, a second analyst reads through a colleague's report logic line by line to find mistakes. Which technique is this?

options.text: Source validation
Monitoring alert
Data filtering
Peer review

explanation: A peer review has another person inspect the work for errors before it ships. Source validation compares to the origin data, an alert fires on a condition, and filtering narrows the rows.

stem: A calculated field for profit margin divides profit by revenue, but the report shows values above 100 percent. The analyst checks the formula's logic and inputs. Which review is this?

options.text: Calculation review
Source validation
Peer review of branding
Alert tuning

explanation: Reviewing the calculation's logic and inputs finds errors in the formula itself. Source validation checks the origin data, branding review covers appearance, and alert tuning adjusts notification thresholds.

stem: A report that worked yesterday now shows an error for a missing field after the source team renamed a column. Which technique prevents this from recurring?

options.text: Increase the dashboard font size and spacing
Track data structure changes and update mappings
Add a second legend
Reduce the refresh rate

explanation: Following structure changes lets the analyst update field mappings before the report breaks. Fonts, legends and refresh rate do not protect against renamed columns.

stem: A team wants to learn immediately when a nightly refresh fails instead of waiting for users to complain. What should they set up?

options.text: A larger chart on page one
A pie chart of refresh times
A monitoring alert on refresh failure
A footer that lists the report's author

explanation: An alert notifies the team when the refresh fails, so they can react before users see stale data. Charts and footers show information only if someone looks at them.

stem: A report's load time doubles after a developer adds a calculation that scans every row for each visual. Which review would most likely find the cause?

options.text: Branding review of the logo placement
Review of the color palette
Review of the page titles
Code review of the new calculation

explanation: Reading the code reveals the costly row scan and lets the team rewrite it. Logo, palette and title reviews cannot reveal performance problems in a formula.

stem: A weekly report shows a customer count that suddenly drops by 30 percent. Source totals are unchanged, and the analyst suspects a join now drops unmatched rows. Which fix is most appropriate?

options.text: Review the join type and keep unmatched rows
Delete the customer table
Switch the chart to a gauge with a target
Shorten the report title

explanation: Reviewing the join and using one that keeps unmatched rows restores the missing customers. Deleting the table loses data, and a gauge or shorter title does not affect the count.

stem: A date filter works for most users but shows a different range for a team in another time zone. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The chart has too many colors
The filter evaluates dates in a time zone that differs by user
The legend is placed at the bottom of each chart area
The dashboard uses a dark theme

explanation: Date boundaries shift when the filter evaluates in different time zones. Colors, legend position and theme do not change which dates are included.

stem: Users complain that a report is slow only on the tab that shows detail rows for all years. Which design change helps most?

options.text: Add extra detail columns to the table view
Remove the page title from the tab
Show a summary first with drill-through to detail
Enlarge every chart on the tab

explanation: A summary view with drill-through loads a small result first and fetches detail only when needed. Extra columns, titles and larger charts do not reduce the work.

stem: A refresh succeeds, yet report totals include duplicate customer rows after the source added a second feed. Which technique should the analyst apply?

options.text: Increase the refresh frequency of the dataset
Change the theme color
Hide the totals row
Validate the source and remove duplicate records

explanation: Checking the source reveals the extra feed, and removing duplicates restores correct totals. More frequent refreshes would reload the same duplicates, and a theme or hidden totals do not fix them.

stem: A retail report's currency column loads with some values as text, such as 1,250.00, so sums skip them. What is the best correction?

options.text: Convert the column to a numeric type after cleaning
Sort the column alphabetically
Hide the rows that look odd
Add a text label on the chart

explanation: Converting to a numeric type, after removing formatting characters, lets aggregations include every value. Sorting, hiding rows and labels leave the text values unusable in sums.

stem: A data steward wants a warning whenever the daily row count of a source table falls more than 20 percent below its average. What should be created?

options.text: A new report theme
A threshold-based monitoring alert
A manual weekly printout
A longer dashboard title

explanation: A threshold alert triggers automatically when the row count drops past the defined limit. Themes, printouts and titles do not notify anyone in time.

stem: A slicer for Product Category shows a blank entry and filters out rows with missing categories. How should the analyst keep those rows selectable?

options.text: Delete the slicer from the report page
Change the page orientation to landscape
Replace missing categories with an Unknown value
Sort the categories by their name length

explanation: Filling gaps with a labeled value keeps those rows selectable instead of lost. Deleting the slicer, changing orientation and sorting do not address missing values.

stem: A team is unsure whether a margin measure is right, so a colleague who did not write it traces the logic with test values. What is this technique?

options.text: Font and color theme planning
Slicer layout planning with users
Scheduled refresh caching
Calculation review with a peer

explanation: An independent person tracing the logic with known inputs combines calculation review with peer review. The other options are theme, layout and caching choices, and none of them tests a formula.

stem: A report loads slowly because it pulls full detail from a very large source. Which TWO changes would most reduce load time?

options.text: Aggregate data to the needed level
Remove unused columns before load
Add more detailed visuals
Turn on 3D chart effects
Increase the font size

explanation: Aggregating and dropping unused columns both shrink the data the report must load. More detailed visuals add queries, 3D effects add rendering work, and a larger font does nothing for load time.

stem: A scheduled dataset refresh runs too long and sometimes fails. Which TWO actions are most likely to help?

options.text: Add extra calculated columns
Use incremental refresh
Load all history each night
Partition the table and refresh only recent partitions
Rename every field

explanation: Incremental refresh loads only changed data, and partitioning limits each run to recent partitions, so runs are shorter and less likely to fail. Extra columns add work, reloading all history is the slow approach, and renaming fields has no effect on duration.

stem: A report shows stale numbers. Which TWO checks should the analyst make first?

options.text: Whether the scheduled refresh succeeded
Whether the logo is current
Whether the source itself was updated
Whether the chart has a legend
Whether the theme is dark

explanation: Stale data comes from a failed refresh or from a source that has not changed. A logo, a legend and a theme are cosmetic and cannot make numbers old.

stem: A filter returns fewer rows than expected. Which TWO causes are plausible?

options.text: Values with trailing spaces
A chart title that is too short
A page with a light background
A legend on the right
A column stored as the wrong data type

explanation: Hidden spaces and mismatched data types stop values from matching the filter. A short title, a light background and a legend position have no effect on which rows pass.

stem: Which THREE are examples of review techniques used to validate a report before release?

options.text: Code review
Calculation review
Chart recoloring
Font resizing
Logo swapping
Peer review

explanation: Code, calculation and peer reviews each inspect the logic or work for errors. Recoloring, resizing and swapping a logo change appearance and do not validate anything.

stem: A file load produced corrupt text values. Which TWO steps help find and fix the problem?

options.text: Compare the file to the original export
Add a trendline
Change the page layout
Re-import with the correct encoding
Enlarge the dashboard

explanation: Comparing to the original export confirms the corruption, and re-importing with the right encoding repairs it. A trendline, layout change or larger dashboard leaves the stored values unchanged.

stem: A vendor renamed two source columns, and the report broke. Which TWO practices reduce the chance of this recurring?

options.text: Hide all report errors
Track source structure changes
Use larger chart fonts
Alert on refresh errors
Remove the data model

explanation: Tracking structure changes warns the team in advance, and error alerts reveal breaks quickly. Hiding errors masks the problem, fonts are irrelevant, and removing the model destroys the report.

stem: Which TWO are benefits of a monitoring alert on a nightly refresh?

options.text: The team learns of failures quickly
Report colors update on their own
Source columns are renamed automatically
Chart types are chosen for the user
Stale data is caught before users see it

explanation: An alert tells the team about a failure fast, so the stale data can be corrected before users notice. Alerts do not change colors, rename columns or choose chart types.

stem: A dashboard is slow on first load. Which THREE changes would most likely help?

options.text: Limit the visuals per page
Add more slicers to the layout
Cache results for repeat viewers
Pre-aggregate large tables
Show detail rows for every year
Use bigger images

explanation: Fewer visuals, cached results and pre-aggregated tables all cut the work done at load. More slicers and detail rows add queries, and bigger images add download size.

stem: The sales dashboard did not update overnight. Review the refresh log, then complete each step.

output: 03:00:03 INFO  source query started: fact_sales (41,200,000 rows)
03:14:50 WARN  source query slow: 887 s elapsed
03:15:02 ERROR source query timeout after 900 s
03:15:02 ERROR refresh failed; dashboard keeps data from 2026-10-28

steps.label: Type a command that shows every ERROR line in refresh_sales.log

options.text: Expired credentials for the data source
The source query reads too many rows and times out
Too many visuals on the report page
A slicer is set to the wrong region
Keep the full reload and raise the timeout every week
Refresh only new or changed partitions each night
Hide the last-refreshed date on the dashboard
Delete the dataset and rebuild it by hand

explanation: The log shows a slow query that hits a timeout, so the refresh fails and old data stays. Refreshing only changed partitions shrinks the work; credentials and slicers do not cause a timeout, and hiding the date only conceals stale data.

partExplanations.find: grep ERROR refresh_sales.log prints only the ERROR lines.
partExplanations.cause: The WARN and ERROR lines name a source query timeout.
partExplanations.fix: Incremental refresh reduces the rows read each night.

stem: Use the refresh times to answer each question.

options.text: 12 minutes
18 minutes
90 minutes
11 minutes
12 minutes
18 minutes

explanation: The total is 10 + 12 + 11 + 45 + 12 = 90, so the mean is 18. Sorted, 10, 11, 12, 12, 45 gives a median of 12, and Thursday is 45 - 12 = 33 minutes above it.

stem: A region filter on a report drops rows it should keep. Put the troubleshooting steps in order.

steps.text: Reproduce the problem and note the expected row count
Check the region values in the source for spelling variants first
Then check how the filter is scoped and which visuals it affects
Correct the cause in the source or the filter
Retest and compare the totals with the source

explanation: Reproduce first, then inspect data and configuration, fix the cause, and confirm against the source.

partExplanations.s1: A known expected count makes the problem measurable.
partExplanations.s2: Source values are the most common cause.
partExplanations.s4: Fix only once the cause is known.

stem: Match each report problem to the best technique for catching or fixing it.

fields.label: The nightly refresh silently stops and owners learn days later

options.text: Monitoring alert on refresh failure
Peer review of the layout
Add a legend

fields.label: A page that pulls 90 million detail rows takes three minutes to open

options.text: Change the heading font
Aggregate to the grain the page needs
Add a monitoring alert

fields.label: A margin measure divides by the wrong column

options.text: Take a snapshot
Switch to real-time data
Calculation review by a peer

explanation: An alert tells owners about a failed refresh, aggregation cuts the volume a page loads, and a second person checking the formula catches a wrong divisor. The other options do not address those causes.

partExplanations.stale: Only an alert reports a silent failure promptly.
partExplanations.slow: Loading less detail speeds the page.
partExplanations.calc: A peer can spot a wrong column in a formula.

stem: A report page opens very slowly. Select every element likely to be a cause of the slow load.

nodes.text: Chart of 14 months from a summary table
Table loading 2 million detail rows at once
Visual running its own 5-minute query on raw rows

spots.name: Chart of 14 months from a summary table
Table loading 2 million detail rows at once
Visual running its own 5-minute query on raw rows

explanation: Plotting every transaction, loading millions of rows and running a long raw query all add heavy load. A summary chart, a small slicer and a logo are cheap.

partExplanations.table: Two million rows at once is heavy.
partExplanations.custom: A five-minute query dominates load time.
partExplanations.logo: A static image costs almost nothing.

stem: Place the validation technique that best protects each point in the reporting pipeline.

nodes.text: Source tables that may hold corrupt values

explanation: Each stage has a matching check: validate the source for corruption, alert on job failures, review calculations and test the filters. A brand review concerns appearance, not data correctness.

partExplanations.z1: Corrupt values are found by checking the source.
partExplanations.z2: Job failures are caught by alerts.
partExplanations.z3: A calculation is checked by reviewing it.
partExplanations.z4: A slicer is checked by testing what it removes.

stem: Sort each symptom by the kind of problem it points to.

items.text: The page takes two minutes to open
The refresh runs for six hours
The extract has grown to 40 gigabytes
Totals on the dashboard do not match the source
A date column contains the text N/A in some cells
A region filter hides half of the rows

explanation: Load time, refresh time and data volume are about speed and size. Mismatched totals, corrupt values and a faulty filter all make the numbers wrong.

partExplanations.i1: Slow opening is a load-time issue.
partExplanations.i2: A long refresh is a speed issue.
partExplanations.i3: Growth in size is a volume issue.
partExplanations.i4: Totals that differ from the source are a correctness problem.
partExplanations.i5: Text in a date column is corruption.
partExplanations.i6: A filter that drops rows gives wrong results.
